headline: Approved $1,000,000 school repair funding, ADA grant spending, Rail Trail transfer, utility items, and multiple handicapped parking spots.
summary: The City Council approved a reduced $1,000,000 appropriation for school repairs, a $232,000 ADA improvement grant, and a $280,400.65 transfer to the Rail Trail project. It also approved several National Grid utility pole installations, a Verizon utility easement, and a block of handicapped parking requests, while tabling a junk dealer permit renewal and withdrawing two other items.
decisions: Approved two sets of minutes (12/04/2025 Special and Regular Meetings) by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 479/25, a $1,000,000 appropriation (reduced from $2,000,000) for the Schematic Design Phase of the MSBA Accelerated Repair Program, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 480/25, authorization to expend $232,000.00 for the MA Office on Disability FY26 ADA Improvement Grant, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 482/25, a $280,400.65 appropriation transfer from Free Cash to the Rail Trail Project Account, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved a motion to order a public hearing on DOC # 484/25, creation of an 'Energy Advocate' position ordinance, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 485/25, disclosure of a conflict by Jennifer Duran, Asst City Clerk, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 486/25, disclosure of a conflict by Maria Vidal, Asst Tax Assessor, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved a motion to order a public hearing on DOC # 491/25, installation of conduit at Lowell Street, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 492/25, a utility easement grant to Verizon, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 298/25, installation of a JO pole and mid-span pole on Mt Vernon St at Crestwood Circle, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 299/25, installation of a JO pole and mid-span pole on Mt Vernon St near James St, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 407/25, installation of a JO pole on Berkeley Street near Montgomery Street, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 410/25, installation of a JO pole on Brookfield Street near Bowdoin Street, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 411/25, installation of a JO pole on Shepard Street near Glenn Street, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 412/25, installation of a JO pole on Andover Street near Tewksbury and Coolidge Streets, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved a motion to waive the reading of the preamble of the handicapped parking legal notice, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved a motion to take the handicapped parking items as a block, by unanimous voice vote.

Approved the block of handicapped parking documents (DOC # 399/25, 401/25, 402/25, 403/25, 404/25, 424/25, 438/25, 439/25, 440/25, 460/25, 461/25, 462/25, 463/25) and waived the 30-day waiting period only for DOC # 460/25, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 476/25, removal of handicapped parking at 76 Inman Street, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 443/25, child care parking at 11 Platt Street, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved a motion to table DOC # 396/25, the Auto Recycles Group junk dealer permit renewal, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved a motion to withdraw DOC # 477/25, removal of handicapped parking at 25 Durham Street, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved a motion to withdraw DOC # 23/26, confirmation of Charlinett Pascual as Director of Community Development, by unanimous voice vote.
Referred New Business items 009/26 through 021/26 to the Ordinance Committee.
Referred item 022/26, an update on LRA property transfer litigation, to the Economic Development Committee.
Referred item 024/26, authorization to expend $1,649,561 from a MassDOT Chapter 130 grant, to the Budget and Finance Committee.

MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING 
OF THE LAWRENCE CITY COUNCIL 
Tuesday, January 20, 2026 
 
A REGULAR MEETING of the Lawrence City Council was held on Tuesday, January 20, 
2026. The meeting was called to Order at 7:10 p.m. by City Council President, Jeovanny 
Rodriguez. This public meeting of the Lawrence City Council was conducted in person at 
Lawrence City Hall, 200 Common Street and via remote participation. Members of the public 
who attended this meeting were allowed to make comments during the portion of the meeting 
designated for public comment.  
 
He then asked the City Clerk, Eileen Bernal to call the roll:  
Councilor Rosaly Gonzalez [District B] – Present 
Councilor Franklin Miguel [District A] – Present  
Councilor Vivian Marmol [District D] – Present 
Councilor Stephany Infante [District E] – Present 
Councilor Celina Reyes [Councilor at Large] – Present 
Councilor Gregory Delrosario [District C] – Present 
Councilor Marc Laplante [District F] – Present 
Council Vice President, Ana Levy [Councilor at Large] – Present  
Council President, Jeovanny Rodriguez [Councilor at Large] – Present  
Present - 9. Quorum established.   
 
The Council President led the assembly in a Moment of Silence and the Pledge of Allegiance.  
Council Vice President Ana Levy made a Motion to approve the following two (2) sets of 
Minutes:  
12/04/2025  Special Meeting  
12/04/2025 Regular Meeting  
Her motion was seconded by Councilor Celina Reyes. There was no discussion on the Motion 
and it PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote.  
PUBLIC PARTICIPATION:  
 
The City Council President stated that members of the Public who had signed in for Public 
Participation would be allotted two and a half minutes to speak. He noted that their comments 
should be addressed to the Council  as a whole and not to any individual member. Those 
participating were:  
 
H. Maali, 53 Chester Street. Mr. Maali stated that the citizens support the Police Unions. He 
noted that under the impeccable leadership of Chief Aguiler, the Police Department was doing 
well. He also spoke in support of the DPW and the Inspectional Services Department and 
encouraged the city to hire more inspectors. He commended the Public Schools and the 
leadership of Superintendent Ralph Carrero. He praised the Lawrence Teachers and their Union.
Page # 2 
He thanked the Veterans and encouraged the city to hire two new employees in veteran services. 
He encouraged them to activate the council on aging, and to pay the long-term employees as 
much as the new hires. He also spoke in support of Fire Chief Delaney who is doing the best job. 
“Lawrence Always Strong, Always United.”  
 
Richard Russell, 34 Cross Street. Former City Councilor Richard Russell expressed his concern 
with parking of private vehicles in the city owned parking lot at the General Donovan School. He 
noted that many residents struggle to find parking during the winter when the parking restrictions 
are in place to allow for snow removal.  
 
Marc Laplante, 29 Durso Avenue. City Councilor Marc Laplante spoke about the Lawrence 
Square Dedication project. He noted that the square honoring World War II Veteran Richard 
“Rick” Dizazzo would occur on January 22, 2026. He recalled that Mr. DiZazzo was an 
outspoken resident and political activist, known to be animated and unfiltered. While the 
Councilor spoke warmly of the honoree, he also credited him with being the reason the Council 
had to modify their Council Rules in 1999 to add a “civility” clause for Public Participation  
 
No other individual sought to address the Council via Public Participation and the Council 
President submitted the names of the Participants to the City Clerk to be preserved as part of the 
record.   
 
The Council President then invited Councilor Infante, in her capacity as Chair of the Budget and 
Finance Committee, to give the Committee Report.  
Budget and Finance Committee:  
DOC # 479/25 Appropriation of Funds [$2,000,000] for Schematic Design Phase, 
Massachusetts School Building Authority Accelerated Repair 
Program – Odanis Hernandez, Chief Operating Officer, Lawrence 
Public Schools  
The City Council President asked Councilor Stephany Infant, in her capacity as Chair of the 
Budget and Finance Committee to give the Committee Report. Councilor Infante reported that 
the Document came up from Committee with a favorable recommendation to Approve and she 
made that report in the form of a Motion to Approve the Appropriation. Her Motion was 
seconded by Councilor Vivian Marmol. Councilor Infante noted that the original amount 
requested was amended and reduced from $2,000,000 to $1,000,000. She noted this as part of the 
Committee Report. It was also noted that these funds would come from FREE CASH.  
Jason Cabrera, the Chief Financial Officer for the Lawrence Public Schools was present and he 
spoke in support of the Document. 
After being granted the floor, Councilor Infante stated that she was grateful to see upgrades and 
improvements being made at the schools in a meaningful way as opposed to “band-aids." She 
referenced the presentation made by the School Department that outlined the three schools 
involved and the specific repairs to be made to each facility.
Page # 3 
After being granted the floor, Councilor Delrosario echoed the comments of Councilor Infante. 
As there was no further discussion on the matter, the Council President called the question. As 
there was no further discussion on the Document, the Council President called the question. With 
all nine councilors being present and participating, the Motion to Approve DOC # 479/25 
PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote.  
DOC # 479/25 MOTION TO APPROVE   PASSED  
 
DOC # 480/25 Auth to Expend [$232,000.00] MA Office on Disability FY26 ADA 
Improvement Grant – Richard Rodriguez, ADA Coordinator  
Councilor Infante, in her capacity as Chair of the Budget and Finance Committee, noted that 
DOC # 480/25 came up from Committee with a favorable recommendation to approve the item 
and she made that report in the form of a Motion to Approve. Her Motion was seconded by 
Councilor Celina Reyes.  
After being granted the floor, Councilor Laplante asked if there was a time frame in mind for the 
improvements. He stated that some patrons might want to go to view the facility before the 
changes occurred. Richard Rodriguez, the ADA Coordinator was present and he stated that the 
time frame would be set by the Library and he did not know if that was established yet.  
As there was no further discussion on the Document, the Council President called the question. 
The Motion to Approve DOC # 480/25 PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote.  
DOC # 480/25 MOTION TO APPROVE   PASSED

Director

Councilor Levy.  
The Planning Director, Dan McCarthy was present to answer any questions if needed.  
There was no discussion on the Document, and the Council President called the question. The 
Motion to Approve DOC # 482/25 PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote.

Council Vice President Ana Levy, in her capacity as Chair of the Ordinance Committee, noted

Alex Marrero, a consultant for Verizon, was present and spoke on behalf of the matter. He noted

DOC # 396/25 Auto Recycles Group, LLC - Junk Dealer Permit [JDC25-000001] 
48-50 Medford Street – Daniel O’Brien [Re-Tabled] 01-20-2026  
Dan O’Brien, the principal of Auto Recycles Group, LLC was present at the meeting. He stated 
that per the request of the Council he installed 305 feet of chain link fencing at his establishment. 
He also had photos of the fencing for the Council to view. Mr. O’Brien stated that he anticipated 
that the privacy slats for this fencing would be installed within the next week.  
The Council President noted that this business is located within District D and there was a desire 
to make sure that the District D Councilor was satisfied with the work. He also acknowledged 
that the installation of quality fencing (as opposed to the sheet metal that was previously used as 
improvised fencing) was an improvement, but he wanted to make sure that this was enough. He 
noted that there are still portions of the property owned by this business that use concrete blocks 
and sheet metal as fencing.  
After being granted the floor, Councilor Infante stated that she did not want to cause the business 
to cease working. It was noted that the businesses current Junk Dealer Permit as issued was 
expired and the business was still continuing to operate.   
After being granted the floor, Councilor Marmol noted that this business is located in her district. 
She expressed a desire to meet with ISD and reviewing the issues at the location prior to issuing 
the renewed license. Based on that comment, Councilor Infante noted that this might need to be 
tabled.  
Councilor Marmol then made a Motion to Table the Document. Her Motion was seconded by
